name: Go
summary: The language Docker, Kubernetes and Terraform chose: little syntax to memorise, a lot of software to build.
prerequisites: None. This course teaches the language from scratch — it is the entry point for anyone who has never written Go.
syllabus: Composite types: arrays, slices, maps and structs
Functions, closures and pointers without arithmetic
Generics: generic functions and types with constraints
Errors as values, modules and project organisation

topics.title: Why Go exists: fast compilation, a single binary and simplicity
The history of the language and the release cycle
Installation, GOPATH, workspace and the `go` command
First program, `go run` and the built-in documentation
Variables and constants: `var` versus `:=`
Zero values, `const`, `iota`, scope and shadowing
Numeric types: signed and unsigned integers, floats and complex numbers
Booleans, runes and the difference between byte, rune and character
Strings: raw and interpreted literals, immutability and UTF-8
Type conversion and why Go never converts on your behalf
Arrays versus slices: what is actually passed around
Slices from the inside: capacity, growth and `make()`
Converting between slice and array in both directions
Maps, the comma-ok idiom and the unordered map
Structs, struct tags and JSON serialisation
Embedded structs: composition without inheritance
Loops: `for`, `for range`, walking maps and strings
Control flow: `break`, `continue`, labels and the discouraged `goto`
Conditionals: `if`, `if-else` with an initialiser and `switch` without fall-through
Functions: parameters, multiple returns and named returns
Variadic and anonymous functions, and closures
Pass by value: what that means in Go
Pointers: the basics, with structs, with maps and slices
An overview of memory management and the garbage collector
Methods versus functions: when a receiver makes sense
Pointer and value receivers: the choice that changes behaviour
Implicit interfaces and the small-interface pattern
The empty interface, `any` and the cost of losing the type
Embedded interfaces, type assertion and `type switch`
Generics: why they arrived and what problem they solve
Generic functions and types, constraints and type inference
Errors as values: the `error` interface and the handling idiom
`errors.New`, `fmt.Errorf` and the wrapping verb
Wrapping and unwrapping errors: `errors.Is` and `errors.As`
Sentinel errors and when to declare one
`panic` and `recover`: the two places where they belong
Call stacks and debugging an error in production
Modules: `go mod init`, `tidy` and `vendor`
Packages, import rules and what a capital letter means
Using third-party packages and publishing a module of your own
